front.title: Resolution of SCITT and W3C Verification Ambiguities via Detached Evidence Profiles

abstract.t: RFC 9942 (COSE Receipts), RFC 9943 (the SCITT architecture), and the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0 provide the foundational architecture for transparent, verifiable statements. Operational ambiguities remain in receipt verification, statement identity, status freshness, and the boundary between what a receipt proves and what a relying party must establish separately. This document maps fifteen documented pain points to constructions in four individual Internet-Drafts (a dual-receipt profile, a detached evidence handoffs model, a reproducible-review method, and a handshake profile). Where none of those drafts applies, it either proposes a construction or names the existing external mechanism, and for every pain point it states which case applies and what gap remains. Delivery is detached: no API integration, standing connection, or middleware is required. This document does not amend RFC 9942, RFC 9943, or any W3C Recommendation. All test vectors are synthetic.
